Known Smooth and Threshold Interactions for Model Comparison

binwise_interaction.Rd

A reproducible simulated dataset with two focal variables, one control, two continuous outcomes, and a binary outcome. The generating rules illustrate different consequences of categorization.

Usage

data(binwise_interaction)

Format

A data frame with 1200 rows and these columns:

id

Integer row identifier.

x, z

Independent uniform draws between -2 and 2.

control

Independent standard normal draws.

expected_outcome

1 + 0.8*x - 0.5*z + 0.9*x*z + 0.4*control.

outcome

The smooth expectation plus independent normal noise with SD 1.2.

expected_threshold

1 + 1.8*(x > 0) - 0.7*z + 1.1*(x > 0)*z + 0.4*control.

threshold_outcome

The threshold expectation plus independent normal noise with SD 1.2.

probability

Inverse logit of -0.4 + 0.6*x - 0.4*z + 0.7*x*z + 0.3*control.

binary_outcome

A Bernoulli draw at the corresponding probability.

Details

The source generator uses seed 9388 and appends this simulation after the five descriptive examples documented in binwise_examples; those datasets are unchanged. All rows are simulated, with no research or personal data. The continuous product term matches the smooth expectation's form. The zero threshold matches the other continuous outcome's form. This intentional design does not imply that either form is universally preferable. Compare model-fit criteria within the same outcome and sample, not across the different outcomes. The known expectations and probability are teaching aids, not model controls.

See also

bin_interact, binwise_examples

data(binwise_interaction)
